rules.heading: 2. Page > 2.1 Paper parameters
rules.excerpt: - **PG-1** Live width is 186 mm on every paper. Letter keeps 186 mm by widening its side margins, so every width formula is paper-independent.

rules.heading: 2. Page > 2.1 Paper parameters
rules.excerpt: - **PG-2** Body height = live height - header height - 6 mm footer - 3 mm gap. With the full 26 mm header this is 236 mm (A4) or 218 mm (Letter). Every row count is computed from body height; no row count is a constant.

rules.heading: 2. Page > 2.1 Paper parameters
rules.excerpt: - **PG-3** The footer never grows. The header never exceeds 26 mm on page 1 and is exactly 12 mm on continuation pages (HD-20).

rules.heading: 2. Page > 2.1 Paper parameters
rules.excerpt: - **PG-4** When header fields are switched off, the freed height is added to the body and rows are recomputed with the same formula (HD-12). Word-problem pages add the freed height to the work area only.

rules.heading: 2. Page > 2.1 Paper parameters
rules.excerpt: - **PG-5** Orientation is portrait. Landscape is allowed only for hands-on measurement pages (RP-170) and for 2-up half-page sheets (two halves side by side with a dashed cut line between them); it swaps the live area to 271 x 186 mm (A4). A half-page is laid out natively at its own available width (PG-13); it is never a scaled-down full page (PG-20).

rules.heading: 2. Page > 2.1 Paper parameters
rules.excerpt: - **PG-6** Print output must be produced at 100% scale. The print dialog shows the note "Print at 100% (no fit-to-page)" whenever a page contains a ruler, generic coins (their diameters are fixed in mm, RP-111) or a cut-out unit strip.

rules.heading: 2. Page > 2.3 Grid sizing
rules.excerpt: - **PG-10** The cell grid is a fixed-height box with `repeat(rows, 1fr)` rows and `repeat(cols, 1fr)` columns. It is never content-sized. Columns always total exactly 186 mm (or the reduced width in PG-13); rows always total exactly gridH.

rules.heading: 2. Page > 2.3 Grid sizing
rules.excerpt: - **PG-11** Rows per page: `rows = min(targetRows, floor((gridH - 1) / hMin))`, and `cellH = min(gridH / rows, hMin x k)`. `hMin` is the section's minimum cell height (from its cell template), `k` is the stretch cap (1.3 for fact rows, probes and K counting rows; 2.0 for horizontal equation rows; stacked-arithmetic, visual, word-problem, mixed and spiral cells fill the grid). Computed once per section and used on every page of that section, so cells are identical from page to page.

rules.heading: 2. Page > 2.3 Grid sizing
rules.excerpt: - **PG-12** Safety: fixed heights on a page total no more than gridH - 1 mm. Content widths fit their cell width minus 0.6 mm. Banded lesson pages, which are content-sized, keep a budget of body - 4 mm.

rules.heading: 2. Page > 2.3 Grid sizing
rules.excerpt: - **PG-13** A page-side strip (skip-count strip, multiples strip, number track) reduces the grid width to 186 - (strip width + 4 mm gap). `resolveSectionLayout` takes the available width as an input; no formula assumes 186.

rules.heading: 2. Page > 2.3 Grid sizing
rules.excerpt: - **PG-14** All spare height in a cell goes to the answer zone (below the sum rule, below the visual, or into the work area). It never goes above the problem.

rules.heading: 2. Page > 2.3 Grid sizing
rules.excerpt: - **PG-15** Trailing empty positions: the generator rounds item counts to full rows. Any remainder is drawn as one unruled blank area inside the closed outer frame, with no interior borders and no labels, so a pupil cannot mistake it for unanswered work.

rules.heading: 2. Page > 2.4 Pagination
rules.excerpt: - **PG-20** Content never shrinks to fit. When content does not fit, in this order: (1) the item count on the page drops and the rest flows to the next page, (2) the column count clamps (DN-10), (3) the page type switches to its two-sided form. Type sizes, writing height, blank widths and minimum visual sizes are never reduced.

rules.heading: 2. Page > 2.4 Pagination
rules.excerpt: - **PG-21** A cell is never split across pages. A band is never split from its first row of cells. A Day band, a word problem, a story box with its diagram, and a Model with its Steps are keep-together units.

rules.heading: 2. Page > 2.4 Pagination
rules.excerpt: - **PG-22** The instruction line repeats at the top of every page on which its section continues, with identical wording.

rules.heading: 2. Page > 2.4 Pagination
rules.excerpt: - **PG-23** If the last page of a row-based section would hold fewer than one third of a full page's rows, rows are rebalanced evenly across the section's pages.

rules.heading: 2. Page > 2.4 Pagination
rules.excerpt: - **PG-24** Continuation pages use the 12 mm continuation header (HD-20) and continue the label sequence.

rules.heading: 2. Page > 2.4 Pagination
rules.excerpt: - **PG-25** On screen, pagination is replaced by vertical scroll; PG-21 still holds for the print preview, which is the real print DOM scaled down.

rules.heading: 7. Companions > 7.2 Anchor chart
rules.excerpt: - **PT-ANC-1.** Zones 110 + 70 + 44 plus two 3 mm gaps = 230 <= 232. The example is the skill's cell at size L drawn at 1.5 x (a poster exception to PT-ENG-1: nothing is written on it).

rules.heading: 7. Companions > 7.2 Anchor chart
rules.excerpt: - **PT-ANC-2.** One picture per rule; arrows point to the one critical spot. Half-page (2-up, cut line dashed) is the desk version.

rules.heading: 4. Fact layouts > 4.5 Cumulative fact review
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CFR-1.** Long form: 24 vertical + 16 horizontal. At L: 9 + 117 + 6 + 103 = 235 (vertical rows 1.3 x 30 = 39; horizontal pitch (220 - 117) / 4 = 25.75 <= 2.0 x 20). Short form: 16 vertical (8 x 2) + 4 horizontal (4 x 1).

rules.heading: 4. Fact layouts > 4.5 Cumulative fact review
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CFR-2.** The title names the range of constants in the Review form ("Review: adding 0 to 7"), and its bracketed constraint names the band when that is not the skill's default ("Review: adding 0 to 7 (sums to 20)"). Facts are drawn evenly from every set in the range, and every answer stays inside the band. No supports.

rules.heading: 3. Practice roles > 3.1 Computation grid
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CGR-1.** Size fixes the digit size; columns only divide the width. A choice above the table maximum, including 7 to 10, clamps with a dialog note (PT-COL-5). Two-digit fact drills that need 7 to 10 columns belong on Fact rows (4.1).

rules.heading: 3. Practice roles > 3.1 Computation grid
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CGR-2.** Any regroup scaffold forces 0.95 em tracks in both looks. Addition and multiplication get regroup boxes above every column except the ones. Subtraction gets a blank headroom row above the top operand; subtraction boxes are offered only at L and only in Model and Guided cells.

rules.heading: 3. Practice roles > 3.1 Computation grid
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CGR-3.** Regroup boxes are square-cornered, solid 0.75 pt. Guided track marks are grey, 1 pt, 2 mm long. Nothing is dashed except the missing-digit box of PT-CGR-9.

rules.heading: 3. Practice roles > 3.1 Computation grid
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CGR-4.** Place-value labels default to bold letters H T O (Th) at label size in a ruled strip above the tracks; the full words appear once, in the Model cell and the vocabulary box. Dialog option: words, letters, none. Words are offered only where a column is at least 14 mm wide.

rules.heading: 3. Practice roles > 3.1 Computation grid
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CGR-5.** The operator never moves next to a shorter operand. Operands are right-aligned; mixed digit lengths share T (PT-ENG-9).

rules.heading: 3. Practice roles > 3.1 Computation grid
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CGR-6.** Decimals: the printed point on the operands always stays; a grey point in the answer row is a hint and drops at level 1. Money: no currency sign prints in a cell (PT-VIS-6).

rules.heading: 3. Practice roles > 3.1 Computation grid
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CGR-7.** Partial-product rows are ruled in Model and Guided cells; Independent cells get open space of the same height.

rules.heading: 3. Practice roles > 3.1 Computation grid
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CGR-8.** Worked model (option): the first cell position holds a Model cell: left half identical to a practice cell, right half at most 3 numbered steps of 4 words or fewer plus the place-value key. It is unscored (PT-LBL-6). At 1 column the steps sit to the right of the stack.

rules.heading: 3. Practice roles > 3.1 Computation grid
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CGR-9. Missing-digit items.** When one digit inside a stacked problem is unknown, its track holds a **dashed** digit box (0.75 pt, short dash 1.5 mm on / 1 mm off, track - 1 wide x Hw tall) in place of the glyph, on the digit's own row. Dashed = unknown, so the box cannot be mistaken for the solid regroup box above the stack (owner ruling 2026-09-19). One unknown digit per item at first, then two. The cell's footprint is unchanged (design standard LS-8, SL-10, VA-7).

rules.heading: 3. Practice roles > 3.6 Chart and table pages
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CHT-1.** Chart cells and table cells are the blanks: no underscores, no inner lines; any write-in cell is at least 12 to 14 mm wide.

rules.heading: 3. Practice roles > 3.6 Chart and table pages
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CHT-2.** Hundred-chart blanks are teacher-set: share (10, 25, 50, 100%) and pattern (random, a row, a column, skip-count multiples). At M and L cells above 99 are not blanked unless the teacher overrides; they print as trace grey instead.

rules.heading: 3. Practice roles > 3.6 Chart and table pages
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CHT-3.** The same graph may be asked about on two days: read-off questions first, compare-and-combine questions second. Questions sit in the band in the skill's cell template, lettered.

rules.heading: 3. Practice roles > 3.6 Chart and table pages
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CHT-4.** Pupils shade bars and draw tallies or X marks; the key and any pre-filled bars use hatch or the flat grey.

rules.heading: 10. Skill x page role compatibility
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CMP-1. Governing rule.** Any skill can appear on any page role. A role never refuses a skill; the skill's `footprint` decides how many items fit, never whether the skill is allowed. What travels into the role is the **configured** skill — the id plus the option values the teacher set (fact constant, band, practice level, pictures, notation, unknown position, simplest form). A role lays that out; it never invents or overrides one of those values (`design/SKILL_CELL_CONTRACT.md` SCC-P14, SCC-P15). Where a role holds something constant — a probe's 15 vertical + 5 horizontal split, a Test at scaffold level 0 — that is a role rule stated in this document, and it is named in the dialog when it overrides nothing the teacher chose.

rules.heading: 10. Skill x page role compatibility
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CMP-2. Fact layouts are additional.** Section 4 roles require `footprint.factLike = true`. A fact-like skill still works on every other role. A skill that is not fact-like and is sent to a fact layout is rerouted to the Computation grid or Equation drill with a dialog note.

rules.heading: 10. Skill x page role compatibility
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CMP-3. Default adapters** guarantee PT-CMP-1 from day one. A family migration replaces adapters with real members; the roles never change.

rules.heading: 10. Skill x page role compatibility
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CMP-4.** `coverage()` in the cell registry must show every skill x every role rendering without overflow at S, M and L in both looks; the compliance harness fails a migrated family that is red.

rules.heading: 10. Skill x page role compatibility
rules.excerpt: - **PT-CMP-5. Every skill on every role has an answer sheet.** The facsimile answer key (7.1) is a base companion of every role in sections 2 to 8, for every skill, migrated or not. `coverage()` therefore checks `state: answered` as well as `blank` for every skill x role pair, and a pair whose key cannot be rendered is red in the same way as an overflow (PT-KEY-1, PT-KEY-7).

rules.heading: 1. Shared page grammar > 1.6 Columns and size
rules.excerpt: - **PT-COL-1. One rule.** Size fixes the writing space and the top digit size. Columns may move digits only along the section type's ladder. Past the ladder floor the column count clamps.

rules.heading: 1. Shared page grammar > 1.6 Columns and size
rules.excerpt: - **PT-COL-2. Ladders.**

rules.heading: 1. Shared page grammar > 1.6 Columns and size

Content is never shrunk to keep five bands.

rules.heading: 5. Review roles > 5.4 Daily 4

rules.heading: 5. Review roles > 5.4 Daily 4
