rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric
rules.excerpt: | Q-1 | Problem types enumerated | The skill lists its problem types as named `variants[]` (3-5 where the reference sites show that many); each can be requested alone. | Auto |

rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric
rules.excerpt: | Q-2 | Difficulty ladder | The variants and constraints can be ordered from concrete to abstract, and each ladder step that uses the skill maps to a reachable constraint set. | Manual |

rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric
rules.excerpt: | Q-3 | Honours Max Number | Every generated number respects `state.range` (10, 20, 50, 100, 500, 1,000, 10,000), except fixed-domain skills (time, angles, coordinates), which declare `fixedDomain: true`. | Auto |

rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric
rules.excerpt: | Q-4 | Honours Decimal Places | Operands and answers use exactly `state.decimalPlaces` places where the skill supports decimals; otherwise the skill declares that it ignores the setting. | Auto |

rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric
rules.excerpt: | Q-5 | Small numbers available | At range 10 or 20 the skill still generates valid, non-degenerate items (P-12). | Auto |

rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric
rules.excerpt: | Q-6 | Edge cases seeded | The skill declares `edgeCases[]`; a seeded set of 6+ contains at least one (P-10). | Auto |

rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric
rules.excerpt: | Q-7 | Non-examples | Identify / classify / rule skills generate non-examples at 1:3 to 1:1, including near misses. | Auto |

rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric
rules.excerpt: | Q-8 | No answer leaks | The answer does not appear in the question text, the visual, a label, an `alt` / `title` attribute, a data attribute, or the hint. Counts printed as self-check badges are allowed only where the task is not to count. | Auto + Manual |

rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric
rules.excerpt: | Q-9 | Answers recomputed | An independent recomputation matches `q.ans` for every sample; equivalent forms (fractions, times, units) are accepted by the answer check. | Auto |

rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric
rules.excerpt: | Q-10 | Duplicates | At most 10% duplicate items in a set of 20 where the item space allows; never two identical items side by side. | Auto |

rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric
rules.excerpt: | Q-11 | No silent mixing | With one variant and notation requested, 100% of items match (P-28). | Auto |

rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric
rules.excerpt: | Q-12 | Distractors from real misconceptions | `wrongAnswer(q)` and multiple-choice options come from a declared misconception list (table below), are distinct from the answer and from each other, and are plausible in size. | Auto + Manual |

rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric
rules.excerpt: | Q-13 | Reading-load cap | Instruction from the library, at most 12 words; stories within P-WP-17 to P-WP-19; no sentence for the pupil to write. | Auto |

rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric
rules.excerpt: | Q-14 | Both orientations | Computation and fact skills generate vertical and horizontal forms on request (P-16). | Auto |

rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric
rules.excerpt: | Q-15 | Every unknown position | Equation and word-problem skills generate every position in the table of section 8.3 on request. | Auto |

rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric
rules.excerpt: | Q-16 | Worked steps | `workedSteps(q)` is non-empty, 3-6 steps, each within P-5, and the final marks equal the answer. | Auto |

rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric

rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric
rules.excerpt: | Q-18 | Works on every page role | The skill renders on every role in P-27 at S / M / L in both looks without overflow or shrinkage. | Auto |

rules.heading: 12. Content-quality rubric
rules.excerpt: | Q-19 | Print and screen parity | Same cell, same response mode, inputs for blanks (P-29); feedback follows section 11.3. | Auto + Manual |

A Model cell is the only place a completed response may be drawn, and there it is grey or dotted.

rules.excerpt: | RP-04 | Percent of a number; find the whole | 6 | RL-15 bar model split in 10 parts; predict-then-check frame | 2 columns | check-box (prediction), write | `percent_of_number`, `find_whole_from_pct` |

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.1 Rules for every drawing
rules.excerpt: - **RP-5** Any part a pupil shades, colors, counts by touching, or writes in is at least 6 mm in its smaller dimension (also guarantees INK-20).

rules.heading: 1. Problem-type catalogue by domain > 1.12 Ratio and percent (`conversions`)
rules.excerpt: | RP-05 | Write a ratio; equivalent ratios | 6 | RL-01 two object kinds; RL-15 bars | cells 2x3 | template (`__:__`), write | `ratio_intro`, `equiv_ratios` |

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.1 Rules for every drawing
rules.excerpt: - **RP-6** Labels inside a visual use zone-label size; printed targets and prompts (for example the time to draw) use working digit size.

rules.heading: 1. Problem-type catalogue by domain > 1.12 Ratio and percent (`conversions`)
rules.excerpt: | RP-06 | Ratio table; double number line | 6 | table; RL-12 double line | rows / table | table-fill, write | `ratio_tables`, `double_num_line` |

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.1 Rules for every drawing
rules.excerpt: - **RP-7** Art is functional only. No scenery, faces, characters or decoration. At most one illustration on a Model word problem; none on independent items.

rules.heading: 1. Problem-type catalogue by domain > 1.12 Ratio and percent (`conversions`)
rules.excerpt: | RP-07 | Unit rate | 6 | two-row table with a "per 1" column | cells 2x2 | write + unit word | `unit_rate_intro` |

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.1 Rules for every drawing
rules.excerpt: - **RP-8** Every visual exposes its required width and height and a `fits(zoneW, zoneH)` test to the layout engine. If `fits` fails, the generator regenerates the problem with smaller quantities; it never overlaps or shrinks.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.3 Ten frame
rules.excerpt: - **RP-10** 2 x 5 grid, border 1.5 pt, interior 0.75 pt. Horizontal (5 wide) by default and whenever it sits over an equation; vertical (2 wide) when two frames stand side by side.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.3 Ten frame
rules.excerpt: - **RP-11** Counters are circles at 0.65 of the cell, filled left to right, top row first. Set A solid black, set B hollow 0.75 pt. Counters the pupil must draw are absent in Independent, dotted in the first Guided cell. A moved counter in a Model is shown with a small X on the origin and a dotted arrow (first items only).

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.4 Counters and counting pictures
rules.excerpt:
- **RP-20** Two object sets; the teacher picks one per section in the dialog ("Objects: counters / pictures"):
  - **Plain counters** (age-neutral; the default at every Level, P-31): dots, squares, ten-frame counters.
  - **Eight in-house line-art pictures**: star, apple, fish, car, ball, flower, turtle, block. Drawn in-house on one 24 x 24 unit grid, 1.5 pt outline, 0.75 pt interior detail, no fill, no faces, no text.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.4 Counters and counting pictures
rules.excerpt: - **RP-21** One kind of object per cell, in tidy rows of at most 5, left-aligned, equal pitch (item + 3 mm), subitising gap of 1.5 mm extra after the 5th item in a row of 10.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.4 Counters and counting pictures
rules.excerpt: - **RP-22** A dot mat is a rounded rectangle with a vertical 0.75 pt divider. Tally marks are 0.75 pt strokes 6 / 8 / 10 mm tall at 2.5 mm pitch with a diagonal fifth; the tally box is a square-cornered box (it is a writing place).

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.5 Base-10 blocks
rules.excerpt: - **RP-30** **Gridded** (default in Model and charts): unit = u x u square, 0.75 pt outline; rod = u x 10u, vertical, 0.75 pt outline with 0.5 pt segment lines, pitch u + 1; flat = 10u x 10u with 0.5 pt grid; thousand = oblique cube, front face gridded. Loose units are arranged 2 wide x 5 high.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.5 Base-10 blocks
rules.excerpt: - **RP-31** **Quick-draw** (default where the pupil draws): open square = hundred, vertical stick = ten, open dot = one, all 1.5 pt. A printed key shows the three symbols once per page in the Model or Vocabulary band.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.5 Base-10 blocks
rules.excerpt: - **RP-32** Blocks inside a labelled place-value chart sit in their own columns; an empty column is left empty to show zero (never a drawn "0 blocks" mark). Order is always largest place at the left.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.6 Place-value chart
rules.excerpt: - **RP-40** Heavy 1.5 pt outline, 0.75 pt interior, 2-9 columns. Heads row in words when columns are 14 mm or wider, otherwise letters (VA-30). The thousands comma is pre-printed on the column boundary. A decimal chart prints the point on its boundary at working digit size.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.6 Place-value chart
rules.excerpt: - **RP-41** A rounding scaffold prints the target place's head letter in bold with a 1.5 pt divider to its right; nothing marks which way to round.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.7 Number line and hops
rules.excerpt: - **RP-50** Axis 1.5 pt with solid arrowheads at both ends (one end only when the line starts at 0 and the context is whole numbers). Whole / labelled ticks 5 mm tall at 1.5 pt; part ticks 3 mm tall at 0.75 pt. Labels below the line at zone-label size (working digit size when the number line is itself the problem).

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.7 Number line and hops
rules.excerpt: - **RP-51** Tick pitch at least 6 / 7 / 8 mm wherever the pupil marks a tick or draws a hop. Plotted given points are solid dots 2.5 mm across with an item letter above.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.7 Number line and hops
rules.excerpt: - **RP-52** Hops are arcs above the line, 0.75 pt solid when given, dotted when modelled; the hop size sits above the arc. Hops the pupil must draw are absent.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.7 Number line and hops
rules.excerpt: - **RP-53** Vertical number lines and vertical number strips (rounded box, RP-54) are allowed; zero is at the bottom.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.7 Number line and hops
rules.excerpt: - **RP-54** Skip-count strip / number track: rounded box (radius 3 mm, 1.5 pt outline, 0.75 pt dividers between entries), one entry per cell at 8 / 9 / 10.5 mm pitch, numerals 700 at 11 / 13 / 15 pt. Side form: right edge of the page, top-aligned with the grid, width = widest entry + 4 mm (10 / 10 / 12 mm for 2-digit entries, 14 / 14 / 16 for 3-digit), 4 mm gap. Top form: 10 mm tall under the instruction line, fact rows at 7 or more columns only. Fade states: filled, grey, empty (pupil fills), off. A + or − number track holds at most 20 entries: a 0-to-30 track does not fit the grid at any pitch, so above band 20 the track starts at the largest value on the page and stops 19 below it (`design/PAGE_TYPES.md` PT-FPR-3).

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.7 Number line and hops
rules.excerpt: - **RP-55** Reference number line at the top of the page (support option, Wave 5.2; `data-ws-support="refline"`, `data-ws-band="refline"`): one band under the header rule and above the instruction, on every page of the sheet and on its key (the key's band is the pupil's band). The line runs the live width (186 mm on A4) with 6 mm for the arrowheads; axis, ticks and arrowheads follow RP-50 (1.5 pt axis, labelled and whole ticks 5 mm at 1.5 pt, part ticks 3 mm at 0.75 pt, small ticks 2 mm at 0.5 pt); labels below at zone-label size (9 / 10 / 12 pt), fraction labels stacked with a 1 pt bar, decimal labels in one format (0, 0.5, 1). Type never shrinks: a long range raises the label interval (and thins the ticks), and Auto ends land on the label grid so every label gap is the same. Every label is a reference-scale number (`data-ws-ref="1"`, SUPPORTS §S4.2). Band height (natural, reserved before the page's capacity is worked out): about 13 / 13.5 / 14 mm whole-number, 17 / 18 / 19 mm with fraction labels, +7 mm with hop arrows. A skip-count line counts in a step every number of the page lands on (the items' own step, reduced to their common divisor: 71, 73, 75 lies on a line of ones, not of evens); with a dozen ticks or fewer it labels its ends, otherwise landmarks (every 5th count, or every ten), never every count. A long line of ones is drawn as tens with each one as a small tick. Decimal lines keep tenth small ticks down to 0.85 mm apart (a ruler's millimetres; the half-way tick longer), then fifths, then halves; values within 0–1 or 0–2 (percents read as hundredths) get a line of tenths with hundredth small ticks. A fraction step is used only when fractions are the page. Fraction skills whose items each need their own denominator (fraction operations, improper/mixed, graphing) are not offered the page-wide line. It is a hint scaffold (PEDAGOGY 4.1): off is the fade; test and check pages carry it only when the teacher turns on Hints on tests (P-SC-5). On screen the same drawing sits once above the practice card and once above the online worksheet, in a white bordered box; the quiz draws no supports. The screen line follows the skill of the question on the card, on every path a pupil plays by (a shared link, a queued set, the teacher screen's Start, the dropdowns): each item carries its own category and skill, and the line is the one the teacher set on that skill; a skill without the option draws none. The band never adds a page the line-off sheet does not have, and costs the page no more than its own height: rows first give up their slack above their content (a split section's narrow and full-width parts share the loss), the grid keeps its line-off shape, and where the content leaves no slack the rows that are left stretch (up to FILL_CAP) into the lost row's room. A category pool (mixed addition, mixed subtraction) draws the line only once the teacher sets Start and End, on paper and on screen alike, and then shows that one line on every question.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.8 Number bond and part-whole
rules.excerpt: - **RP-60** Whole box above, part boxes below, joined by 0.75 pt lines. Boxes are square-cornered (writing places), side 14 / 16 / 20 mm. The whole box has a 1.5 pt border, parts 0.75 pt. The unknown box is the empty one; it is never dashed (LS-3). Orientation is fixed per section.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.9 Schema diagrams (word problems)
rules.excerpt: - **RP-70** Bars 10 / 12 / 14 mm tall, 1.5 pt outline; slots inside bars are writing places sized by B(n). The unknown is a solid box or bar with a zone-label `?` in its top-left corner (LS-3); exactly one per diagram. Nothing in a diagram is dashed.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.9 Schema diagrams (word problems)
rules.excerpt: - **RP-71** Diagram part labels are printed (the pupil fills numbers, not words) on v1. On v2 the diagram is absent.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.9 Schema diagrams (word problems)
rules.excerpt: - **RP-72** Diagram proportions are schematic and fixed per schema; bar lengths never encode the actual numbers (that would draw the answer).

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.10 Bar model, array, equal groups, area model
rules.excerpt: - **RP-80** Bar model: as RP-70; a bracket (0.75 pt) spans a total; pupil-drawn bar models get an empty rounded "Draw" box of at least 60 x 30 mm instead.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.10 Bar model, array, equal groups, area model
rules.excerpt: - **RP-81** Array: open circles 0.6 of pitch, 0.75 pt (solid black option for "count the array"); rows and columns straight, 1.5 mm subitising gap after the 5th row and column in arrays over 5. No row / column numerals unless the task is to read them.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.10 Bar model, array, equal groups, area model
rules.excerpt: - **RP-82** Equal groups: rounded group outlines, one kind of object, same arrangement in every group.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.10 Bar model, array, equal groups, area model
rules.excerpt: - **RP-83** Area model: a table with a 1.5 pt outline, a heavy header row and column, `x` in the corner, cells sized as writing places (min B(n) x (Hw + 4)). Proportions are schematic (RP-72).

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.11 Fractions and decimals
rules.excerpt: - **RP-90** Fraction circle: outline 1.5 pt, partitions 0.75 pt, sectors start at 12 o'clock and run clockwise. Fraction bar: outline 1.5 pt, dividers 0.75 pt, shading contiguous from the left. Shaded parts are flat grey (hatch in photocopy-safe mode).

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.11 Fractions and decimals
rules.excerpt: - **RP-91** Fraction cells lay out **side by side**: the printed fraction or the fraction answer stack (12 / 14 / 16 mm wide), a 6 mm gap, then the model. No bottom answer zone.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.11 Fractions and decimals
rules.excerpt: - **RP-92** Values above 1 are normal, not special: improper fractions and mixed numbers are drawn as a row of whole models with a 3 mm gap, and fraction number lines run **past 1** (0 to 2 or 0 to 3 by default from the step where improper fractions are introduced). Whole ticks are heavy, part ticks hairline (RP-50).

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.11 Fractions and decimals
rules.excerpt: - **RP-93** Shade-it and partition-it items: parts are empty; each part is at least 6 mm at mid-radius or across. Denominator caps: circle 8 / 10 / 12 at S / M / L; bar 8 in 3 columns, 12 in 2 columns. Partition items show guide dots on the circumference (dotted semantics), never the partition lines.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.11 Fractions and decimals
rules.excerpt: - **RP-94** Decimal grid: 10 x 10, outline 1.5 pt, interior 0.5 pt with 0.75 pt lines every 5; cell at least 4 mm. Tenths strip: 10 parts, each at least 6 mm wide. Decimal number lines label both forms only in the Model.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.12 Clocks
rules.excerpt: - **RP-100** Analog face: rim circle 1.5 pt at R; inner ring 0.5 pt at 0.90 R; minute ticks 0.90 R to 0.85 R at 0.5 pt; five-minute ticks 0.90 R to 0.80 R at 0.75 pt; numerals 1-12 Andika 700 at 0.12 D (never below zone-label minimum) centred on radius 0.66 R; pivot solid dot radius 1 mm.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.12 Clocks
rules.excerpt: - **RP-101** Hands: hour hand 0.46 R, 2.25 pt; minute hand 0.78 R, 1.5 pt; both with round caps and a solid arrow tip. Told apart by length and weight only. Hour-hand angle = 30h + 0.5m degrees (at 12:30 it sits midway between 12 and 1). At 12:00 the minute hand is drawn on top. Hours are written 12, never 0.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.12 Clocks
rules.excerpt: - **RP-102** Precision depends on diameter: hour and half hour need D >= 26 mm; 5-minute D >= 30; 1-minute D >= 42; draw-the-hands D >= 46. A panel that cannot give the diameter offers only the coarser items. **Half-width panels** (Daily Spiral sections, Daily 4 cells): a 38 mm clock is allowed at S, M and L, only for read-the-time items to the hour, half hour or 5 minutes. 1-minute reading and draw-the-hands items always take the full table 11.2 minimum (46 / 50 / 52) and therefore a full-width panel.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.12 Clocks
rules.excerpt: - **RP-103** Variants: (a) plain face; (b) face ringed by 12 rounded write-in boxes for the minute counts (Model / Guided); (c) outer minute ring 5-55 at 1.14 R, black in Model, grey in Guided, off in Independent; (d) half-shaded face (grey right half) for "half past" models; (e) draw-the-hands face: bold rim, numerals, five-minute ticks, **no hands** (hour hand may be pre-drawn grey in Guided); (f) digital: rounded rectangle 1.5 pt, solid Andika 700 digits, two colon dots, no leading zero, no seven-segment styling.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.12 Clocks
rules.excerpt: - **RP-104** The time answer slot is the two-box `__:__` slot (section 6); AM / PM is a words-to-circle choice beside it.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.13 Generic coins and notes
rules.excerpt: - **RP-110** Coins are **generic**: circles that show only a value. Values 1, 5, 10 and 25 only — and, at the Qatari riyal currency only, 50 (owner ruling Q2, 2026-09-25), drawn the same way at the next RP-111 step, 26.51 mm. No national portraits, buildings, mottoes, edge reeding, dates, or dollar / cent art.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.13 Generic coins and notes
rules.excerpt: - **RP-111** Coins are sized **by value**, never by a national coinage: diameters 17.5 (1), 19.75 (5), 22.0 (10), 24.26 (25) mm at scale 1.0. The 1 is the smallest and the 25 the largest, each step is 2.25 mm, and a bigger coin is always worth more (owner ruling 2026-09-19; this replaces the US relative sizes, in which the 10 was the smallest coin). Scale is 1.0 at M and L, 0.85 at S, 0.8 in half-width spiral and mixed panels. Coins never go smaller, never overlap, never fan.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.13 Generic coins and notes
rules.excerpt: - **RP-112** Drawing: outer rim 1.5 pt, inner ring 0.5 pt at 0.88 r (the double ring distinguishes a coin from a counter), value numeral Andika 700 centred, height 0.40 D. White fill.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.13 Generic coins and notes
rules.excerpt: - **RP-113** Layout: rows, highest value first, 2 mm gaps, each row centred. Independent cells: at most 6 coins per 93 mm cell in up to 2 rows. Model and Guided coin cells are full-width single rows of at most **5** coins, because they carry count-on boxes (a writing box under each coin, Hw + 2 tall) and a running-total zone: five 25s plus gaps is 129.3 mm, leaving 56.7 mm of the 186 mm body, while six would need 155.6 mm and overflow. Six is still allowed in an Independent cell, which has no count-on boxes.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.13 Generic coins and notes
rules.excerpt: - **RP-114** Optional count-by-fives dots (hint scaffold): solid 1.5 mm dots under the numeral, one per five (5: one dot, 10: two, 25: five); the 1 coin carries a short stroke. Off in Independent by default.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.13 Generic coins and notes
rules.excerpt: - **RP-115** Generic notes: upright-format rounded rectangles 60 x 26 mm, 1.5 pt outline, 0.5 pt inset border, value in the centre and in two opposite corners. Not true scale relative to coins. Values 1, 5, 10, 20 at Plain numbers; a currency brings its own notes (Qatari riyal 1, 5, 10, 50, 100, 200, 500; US dollar 1, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100), drawn the same generic way (ruling Q1, 2026-09-25).

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.13 Generic coins and notes
rules.excerpt: - **RP-116** A currency sign or currency word appears only in word-problem story text, and then also beside that problem's blank (SL-9). When a money skill's `currency` is not Plain numbers (owner ruling Q3, 2026-09-25) it may also appear as the unit word after an answer blank ("__ dirhams", "__ cents"), before the money slot on the write-the-amount step (`QR [ ].[ ]`, `$[ ].[ ]`), and left of the top number in money columns. Qatari amounts are written QR; paper money is called "notes" in both currencies. It never appears on a coin, a note, a header, a title or an instruction.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.15 Shapes and solids
rules.excerpt: - **RP-120** A shape to judge or name has a 1.5 pt outline; a shape to shade or partition has a 0.75 pt outline. No fill. Equal-side ticks 0.5 pt; right-angle mark a 3 mm square, 0.5 pt; angle arcs 0.75 pt at radius 8 mm.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.15 Shapes and solids
rules.excerpt: - **RP-121** Orientation varies across a section (not every triangle sits on its base) and every "identify" section includes non-examples.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.15 Shapes and solids
rules.excerpt: - **RP-122** Solids use oblique projection (depth 0.4 at 30 degrees). Visible edges 1.5 pt; hidden edges 0.5 pt solid (LS-2). Cylinder and cone ellipses use ry = 0.3 rx. Unit-cube stacks show every visible cube edge at 0.75 pt.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.15 Shapes and solids
rules.excerpt: - **RP-123** Names are words-to-circle (two choices, stacked on two lines) or label-from-bank. Pupils are not asked to hand-write names longer than 8 letters.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.16 Graphs and data
rules.excerpt: - **RP-130** Axes 1.5 pt; grid 0.5 pt; tick labels and category labels at zone-label size; axis titles in words at zone-label size 700. Scale labels are printed (pupils never invent a scale except on a construct-a-graph item with pre-labelled axes).

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.16 Graphs and data
rules.excerpt: - **RP-131** Bar graph: bars at least 8 mm wide with gaps of at least half a bar. Series 1 grey fill with 1.5 pt outline; series 2 white with 1.5 pt outline; series 3 solid black only if bars are 7 mm wide or less, otherwise hatch 135 is not available in standard mode and the graph is limited to two series. Draw-the-bars items show axes and grid only.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.16 Graphs and data
rules.excerpt: - **RP-132** Pictograph: in-house icons from RP-20, a printed key ("1 picture = 2"), half icons clipped vertically. Line plot: X marks at 0.75 pt, 5 mm, stacked on a number line. Tally table: RP-22. Circle graph: at most 12 sectors, labels outside with leader lines, sectors differentiated by grey / white / labels, never by more than one grey.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.16 Graphs and data
rules.excerpt: - **RP-133** A graph and its questions share one keep-together unit; the graph is never redrawn smaller to make room for more questions.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.17 Hands-on page conventions (later family, specified now)
rules.excerpt: - **RP-140** **Dashed always means cut.** Cut tiles have a dashed 0.75 pt outline, are at least 25 x 20 mm, carry content at cell-text or working digit size, and sit in one block at the foot of the page under a full-width dashed line with a scissors glyph. Nothing else on the page is dashed (LS-4).

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.17 Hands-on page conventions (later family, specified now)
rules.excerpt: - **RP-141** Paste boxes are square-cornered, 0.75 pt, tile size + 2 mm. Two-bin sorts have two labelled bins with equal numbers of paste boxes. Cut-and-order pages have a numbered row of paste boxes.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.17 Hands-on page conventions (later family, specified now)
rules.excerpt: - **RP-142** Match with a line: two columns of items with solid 2.5 mm anchor dots facing each other across a clear channel of at least 40 mm; at most 6 pairs per page at L.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.17 Hands-on page conventions (later family, specified now)
rules.excerpt: - **RP-143** Find-and-color: a rounded count badge near the instruction states how many to find ("Find 8"); targets are at least 12 mm; the pupil uses one crayon color, so nothing depends on which color.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.17 Hands-on page conventions (later family, specified now)
rules.excerpt: - **RP-144** Layered place-value strips: strips of graded length (ones shortest), right-aligned when stacked, each with a grey left tab for stapling. **Exception to the working-digit-size rule (section 3.2, TY-10, RP-140):** poster-size digits are allowed on cut-and-layer strips, and nowhere else: 63 pt, one digit per 40 mm unit track (geometry in `design/PAGE_TYPES.md` 8.6).

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.17 Hands-on page conventions (later family, specified now)
rules.excerpt: - **RP-145** Flashcards: 3 x 3 rounded cards per page (9), dashed cut lines between cards, fact centred at 28 pt, optional cue version (SF-30) as a separate page; backs are blank (single-sided).

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.17 Hands-on page conventions (later family, specified now)
rules.excerpt: - **RP-146** Cut lines never cross a cell's content, and a hands-on page is always printed single-sided (dialog note).

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.14 Ruler and measurement
rules.excerpt: - **RP-160** Rulers print at true scale only (PG-6). Inch ruler: numerals under the ticks, tick heights by fraction (1 in 6 mm, 1/2 4.5, 1/4 3.5, 1/8 2.5). Centimetre ruler: cm ticks 5 mm, half 4, mm 2.5. Body 0.75 pt outline, 14 mm tall, zero tick inset 3 mm from the body's end.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.14 Ruler and measurement
rules.excerpt: - **RP-161** Objects to measure are line art or dotted segments with solid end dots, aligned to the zero tick in Model cells and offset from it only from the step that teaches offset measuring.

rules.heading: 11. Representation drawing rules > 11.14 Ruler and measurement
rules.excerpt: - **RP-170** Hands-on measurement pages (unit strips, ruler hunts) may be landscape (PG-5).

rules.heading: 1. Scope and the two looks > 1.1 Scope
rules.excerpt: - **SC-1** This standard applies to every printed pupil page, every answer key, the print preview, and the black-and-white question region (`.ws-cell`) of every on-screen host: game card, online worksheet, quiz builder preview, quiz taking, skills navigator preview, classroom export preview and map engine.

rules.heading: 1. Scope and the two looks > 1.1 Scope
rules.excerpt: - **SC-2** It does not style game chrome: XP, levels, boss and race scenes, buttons, toasts, progress bars, and correct / incorrect feedback keep their color. Chrome never enters a cell (section 15).

rules.heading: 1. Scope and the two looks > 1.1 Scope
rules.excerpt: - **SC-3** Governing rule: any skill can appear on any page type (opener, scripted model, guided, independent, more practice, sub-skill / decision, error analysis, review, test A/B, pre-skill check, daily spiral panel, mixed practice, Daily 4, True or False?, Reason It, Stretch, word problem). Fact and operations skills additionally get the high-column fact layouts (fact rows at 5-10 columns, fact probe, fact-family intro / warm-up / probe, practice strips) and must still work on every other page type. No rule in this file may be satisfied by excluding a skill from a page type.

rules.heading: 1. Scope and the two looks > 1.1 Scope
rules.excerpt: - **SC-4** Conventions are US / Common Core: "regroup" (never "carry" or "borrow" in pupil text), customary and metric units, the US long-division bracket, comma thousands separator, decimal point. Pupil-facing strings use US spelling.

rules.heading: 1. Scope and the two looks > 1.1 Scope
rules.excerpt: - **SC-5** Pupil pages say "Level N" (K, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6) and never "Grade N". Grade and CCSS code appear only in the teacher footer (HD-30) and never inside a cell, band, title or tab.

rules.heading: 1. Scope and the two looks > 1.1 Scope
rules.excerpt: - **SC-6** No tracking artefacts are specified or may be added: no goal pages, pupil trackers, class records, mastery logs, progress graphs or mastery gates. A per-page Score line and an optional per-page Goal / Time line (section 8) are the only record fields.

rules.heading: 1. Scope and the two looks > 1.1 Scope
rules.excerpt: - **SC-7** Every page is black, white and one grey (section 4). No color, gradient, shadow, emoji, clip-art, mascot or decorative lettering appears anywhere on a sheet.

rules.heading: 1. Scope and the two looks > 1.2 The two looks
rules.excerpt: - **SC-10** A page uses exactly one look. A packet may mix looks between pages, never inside one page.

rules.heading: 1. Scope and the two looks > 1.2 The two looks
rules.excerpt: - **SC-11** Both looks share every token in sections 2-6 and 8-16. Only the rows of the table above differ.

rules.heading: 0. Conventions, scope and architecture > 0.4 Module map and layers
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-01** The kit (`js/modules/sheet/**`) is pure ES modules. It MUST NOT write to `window`, MUST NOT import
  `state.js`, `storage.js`, `progress.js`, `gamification.js`, `dashboard.js` or any `gen-*.js`, and MUST NOT
  call `Math.random`. Anything it needs from higher layers is injected (section 4.1).

rules.heading: 0. Conventions, scope and architecture > 0.4 Module map and layers
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-02** No pupil data of any kind flows into the kit or the composers. There are no tracker, log, goal or
  mastery page roles, and no role reads saved progress. "Earlier work" on review pages always means skills the
  teacher listed, never stored history.

rules.heading: 0. Conventions, scope and architecture > 0.4 Module map and layers
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-03** New functions called from inline HTML handlers are added to **both** the import line and the
  `Object.assign(window, {...})` block of `js/globals.js`. The kit itself attaches screen behaviour with
  `addEventListener` inside `mountCell`, so it adds no inline handlers.

rules.heading: 0. Conventions, scope and architecture > 0.4 Module map and layers
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-04** No new dependency, CDN entry or build step. Every touched module passes
  `node --input-type=module --check < file.js`.

rules.heading: 0. Conventions, scope and architecture > 0.4 Module map and layers
rules.excerpt: - **SCC-05** Generation is synchronous. No code between installing and restoring the seeded RNG may `await`.

rules.heading: 4. Default adapters: every existing skill works immediately > 4.1 Injection
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-A1** If `installLegacyAdapters` has not run, `getProvider` still returns a provider; the affected members
  return their empty forms (`[]`, `null`, a text-only cell). Tests rely on this.

rules.heading: 4. Default adapters: every existing skill works immediately > 4.2 Cell: the `legacy` template
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-A2** The adapter always passes a **shallow clone** to `formatLegacy`, because the legacy function
  rewrites `problem.text` and `problem.visual` in place (`print-generate.js:3868-3906`). Without the clone a
  second render (key page, thumbnail) double-processes the strings.

rules.heading: 4. Default adapters: every existing skill works immediately > 4.2 Cell: the `legacy` template
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-A3** `columns` is capped at 9 so the ten-column shortcut (`print-generate.js:4028-4042`) never fires
  inside a cell. Real 5-10 column fact rows come from the `fact` template.

rules.heading: 4. Default adapters: every existing skill works immediately > 4.2 Cell: the `legacy` template
rules.excerpt: - **SCC-A4** `showSkillLabels` is always `false`: the kit owns labels.

rules.heading: 4. Default adapters: every existing skill works immediately > 4.2 Cell: the `legacy` template
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-A5** The cell is marked `data-ws-legacy="1"`. The legacy work-space box (`.ws-work-space`,
  `print-generate.js:12042-12044`) is restyled to a solid hairline by one additive rule in `css/sheet-kit.css`,
  so that dashed keeps its single meaning.

rules.heading: 4. Default adapters: every existing skill works immediately > 4.2 Cell: the `legacy` template
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-A6** `footprint` for a legacy cell is `{ measure: true, hMm: null }`. The caller of `paginate` supplies a
  `measure(html)` function (a hidden off-screen `.sheet-page` with the real stylesheets).

rules.heading: 4. Default adapters: every existing skill works immediately > 4.2 Cell: the `legacy` template
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-A7** `display` for the stamp is `String(q.ans)` for simple values, otherwise `answerKeyHint(q)` joined
  with the answer. `inputs` returns the single entry `{ id: 'answer', kind: 'text', shape: 'line', graded: true }`.

rules.heading: 9. `ladders.js`: step objects and how a step constrains a generator > 9.3 Constraints
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-D1** If a constraint is neither supported nor checkable, or rejection runs out, generation for that step
  fails loudly in the dialog. A constraint is never silently relaxed.

rules.heading: 9. `ladders.js`: step objects and how a step constrains a generator > 9.3 Constraints
rules.excerpt: - **SCC-D2** Skills with no ladder keep today's behaviour and still reach every page role.

rules.heading: 5. `generateQuestionFor` > 5.2 Behaviour
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-G1 State swap in try/finally.** Save, set, generate, restore. Restored in `finally`, so an exception in a
  generator can never leave the app in the wrong skill. Swapped keys: `category`, `skill`, `range`,
  `decimalPlaces`, `gameMode`, `isMixedMode`, `difficulty`, `hasAnswered`, `currentQ`, `qCount`, `quizMode`,
  `mapMode`, `adaptiveModeEnabled`, `skillOptions`, and a copy of `selectedNumbers`.

rules.heading: 5. `generateQuestionFor` > 5.2 Behaviour
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-G2 Fixed difficulty.** Inside the swap `adaptiveModeEnabled` and `mapMode` are `false`. The adaptive hook
  at `generate-question.js:83-89` otherwise changes `state.range` whenever `gameMode` is `'practice'`, which is
  what all four existing swap sites set.

rules.heading: 5. `generateQuestionFor` > 5.2 Behaviour
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-G3 `gameMode` stays `'practice'`** by default, to match the four existing sites and the baseline images.
  (It also keeps the fraction-input promotion at `generate-question.js:533-548` behaving as it does today.)

rules.heading: 5. `generateQuestionFor` > 5.2 Behaviour
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-G4 Full payload pass-through.** The function returns the object `generateQuestion()` returned, plus
  `categoryId`, `skillId` (if the generator left it unset), `seed`, `variant`, `notation`, `representation` and
  `ignoredOpts`. There is no field whitelist. The print call site applies `q.printFormat ||= 'horizontal'` as it
  does today (`print-settings.js:1374`).

rules.heading: 5. `generateQuestionFor` > 5.2 Behaviour
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-G5 Seeded RNG.** When `seed` is an integer, `mulberry32(seed)` is installed over `Math.random` and the
  original function is put back in `finally`. `randInt`, `shuffle` and `pick` (`utils.js:3-7`) and every bare
  `Math.random()` in the generators then become reproducible with no generator edits.

rules.heading: 5. `generateQuestionFor` > 5.2 Behaviour
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-G6 What "reproducible" covers.** For the same spec and seed, `q.text`, `q.ans` and
  `JSON.stringify(q.cell.payload)` are identical. `q.visual` is **not** covered: some generators build DOM ids
  from `Date.now()` (`gen-operations.js:983`, `:5179`).

rules.heading: 5. `generateQuestionFor` > 5.2 Behaviour
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-G7 Variant history is isolated.** `pickVariant` keeps least-recently-used history on
  `window.__variantHistory` and `window.__variantWrongCounts` (`variant-cycler.js:45-49`). A seeded call swaps in
  fresh buckets (or the batch's buckets) and restores the live ones in `finally`, so gameplay history neither
  affects nor is affected by sheet generation. The tie-break jitter (`variant-cycler.js:108`) uses
  `Math.random`, so it is seeded too.

rules.heading: 5. `generateQuestionFor` > 5.2 Behaviour
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-G8 Options are honoured only when declared.** For each of `variant`, `notation`, `representation`: if the
  provider declares an option with that id, the pair `{ [cyclerKey]: id }` is forced through the variant cycler.
  If not, the option is dropped and named in `q.ignoredOpts`; the dialog shows it, the sheet does not.
  `scaffoldLevel` is forced under the key `<skillId>#scaffold` and only matters to generators that call
  `pickVariant('<skillId>#scaffold', ['3','2','1','0'])`. For everyone else the level is purely a render-time
  `ctx` value.

rules.heading: 5. `generateQuestionFor` > 5.2 Behaviour
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-G9 Retries.** Up to 3 retries when the result is unusable (`!q || !(q.text || q.visual || q.cell)`), each
  with `deriveSeed(seed, 'retry', n)`. After that, `null`; the caller keeps its fallback
  (`generateCategoryFallbackStatic`, `print-settings.js:1403`).

rules.heading: 5. `generateQuestionFor` > 5.2 Behaviour
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-G10 Aliases first.** The spec passes through `resolveSkill` (section 11.3) before anything else; alias
  options are the base and `spec.opts` overrides them. `generateQuestion()` also resolves aliases for live play
  (`generate-question.js:53-70`); because the wrapper has already resolved, that second pass is a no-op.

rules.heading: 5. `generateQuestionFor` > 5.2 Behaviour
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-G10a One channel for generator-readable options.** Inside the swap, `state.skillOptions` holds the merged
  options (`variant`, `notation`, `representation`, `scaffoldLevel`, `tables`, `constraints`). This is the same
  field the alias redirect in `generateQuestion()` fills (`generate-question.js:57-68`). Generators MAY read it;
  the variant cycler remains the mechanism that actually forces a declared variant, notation or representation.

rules.heading: 5. `generateQuestionFor` > 5.2 Behaviour
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-G11 Seeds.** A sheet has one base seed, shown in the dialog in base 36. Derived seeds:
  `deriveSeed(base, 'section', id)`, then `'item', i`; test forms `'form', 'A'` and `'form', 'B'`; probe versions
  and Today's Number versions `'version', 'A'..'D'`; day bands `'day', n`.

rules.heading: 5. `generateQuestionFor` > 5.5 The four call sites it replaces
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-G12** Switching site 1 to full pass-through wakes print branches that have been starved of data.
  Baseline images of every skill MUST exist before that commit and every difference MUST be reviewed.

rules.heading: 8. Layout routing > 8.2 `q.layout` and `resolveLayout`
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-L1** `legacySniff` reproduces today's decisions exactly, including the precedence of the `if` chain at
  `worksheet.js:1012-1046`. Before it is written, the two copies in `worksheet.js` are diffed; any difference is
  recorded as a finding and the first-render copy wins.

rules.heading: 8. Layout routing > 8.2 `q.layout` and `resolveLayout`
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-L2** Both copies in `worksheet.js`, and `question-render.js:1471`, `:1536-1591` and `:1644-1647`, are
  replaced by a call to `resolveLayout(q)`. The listener attachment at `worksheet.js:1286` and `:1824` switches
  from `isVerticalFormat` to `layout.checker === 'columns'`.

rules.heading: 8. Layout routing > 8.2 `q.layout` and `resolveLayout`
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-L3** `legacySniff` is frozen. New and migrated skills set `q.layout` (or rely on their template). Nobody
  adds a string to it; entries are only ever deleted as families migrate.

rules.heading: 8. Layout routing > 8.2 `q.layout` and `resolveLayout`
rules.excerpt:
- **SCC-L4** Outside `sheet/layout.js` no module may test `q.visual` with `includes`, a regular expression or an
  emoji literal to decide layout or behaviour.

rules.heading: 8. Layout routing > 8.4 Name collision: `q.layout` as a string
